extraction.name: VAP-Data
extraction.description: The largest dataset for semantic-controlled video generation with over 100K curated paired videos across 100 semantic conditions.
extraction.creator: Yuxuan Bian, Xin Chen, Zenan Li, Tiancheng Zhi, Shen Sang, Linjie Luo, Qiang Xu
extraction.publisher: Intelligent Creation Lab, ByteDance, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Collected 2K high-quality reference images from the Internet, spanning men, women, children, animals, objects, landscapes, and multi-subject cases. Then used Image-to-Video visual-effects templates from commercial models (VIDU and Kling) and community LoRAs to create paired videos by matching each image to all compatible templates.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 2K high-quality reference images from the Internet and Image-to-Video visual-effects templates from commercial models (VIDU and Kling) and community LoRAs.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Videos are resized to 480x720 (832) and sampled at 49 frames at 16 fps.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender and age (images spanning men, women, children).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Potential misuses include identity impersonation, deepfake content, targeted harassment, deceptive political messaging, and generation of sexualized or violent media. Mitigations include a research-only release and default content filters blocking clearly harmful categories.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is synthetic and derived from other generative models, which may inherit the specific stylistic biases, artifacts, and conceptual limitations of the source templates (e.g., if the source models are poor at generating hands, the model will likely not learn to generate hands well).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The semantic conditions in VAP-Data are relatively limited, synthetic, and derived from other generative models. It is not intended for surveillance, impersonation, political persuasion, or other high-risk deployments.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Semantic-controlled video generation for research, education, and creative prototyping.
